case_title: Digamber Vaishna & Anr. v. State of Chhattisgarh
accused_victim_relationship: Not stated (court found acquaintance between accused and victims not shown)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34; IPC s.394 r/w s.34
evidence_type: Circumstantial evidence: child witness testimony, s.27 recoveries, fingerprint report, FSL/hair report, alleged robbery motive, last seen together
confession: Section 27 disclosure statements by the accused leading to recoveries (motorcycle, cash, anklet, shirt); the Court did not treat them as a confession and found the recoveries unreliable
aggravating_circumstances: Five women killed by strangulation (as found by the trial court); the Supreme Court weighed no aggravating factor
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302/34 IPC and sentenced to death; convicted under s.394/34 IPC and sentenced to RI for ten years with fine of Rs.500 (default one month RI)
high_court_outcome: Death reference confirmed; criminal appeals dismissed; death sentence affirmed
neutral_facts: Five women living in one house were found dead on 17 December 2012, with some bodies in a courtyard and others in a room. A relative who was alerted by a child living in the house went to the scene and saw blood from the nose and mouth of the victims and marks of injury on their necks. A post-mortem examination found that all five died of asphyxia due to strangulation, and the deaths were homicidal. The investigating officer prepared a site map and seized a glass whisky bottle, a torch, six strands of black hair from one victim's hand, two white buttons, blood-stained soil and a woollen shawl. Fingerprints lifted from the bottle were reported to match one accused. A forensic report found a shirt button and the buttons from the scene to be similar, and a hair report identified only human hair. Following statements made by the accused, a motorcycle, a sum of cash and a silver anklet were recovered, and one accused's shirt was seized. The prosecution alleged that the killings were committed during a robbery. A child witness said that the accused had come to the house the previous night and that, in the early morning, she had found the door locked from outside. She identified the accused as the persons she had seen with the victims. A witness heard of the accused's visit only through a telephone call, and a motorcycle witness gave conflicting descriptions. The gold ornaments and pearl necklace on the victims' bodies were recorded in the site plan.
physical_harm: Death of five women by asphyxia due to strangulation
number_of_offences: 2 charged (s.302 r/w s.34 IPC; s.394 r/w s.34 IPC); 0 finally upheld
financial_property_loss: Not established: cash (Rs.3000 and Rs.2600 recovered) and a silver anklet were alleged to be stolen, but no theft was proved
motive: alleged: robbery (the Court found this motive unsubstantiated)
key_evidence_accepted: None accepted as sufficient to convict; the Court found the chain of circumstances incomplete, including the child witness identification, recoveries, fingerprint and hair evidence, and last seen evidence
witness_credibility: Child witness PW-8 found unreliable: not an eyewitness, inconsistent, contradicted by PWs 1, 3 and 10, and her identification uncorroborated. PW-9 evidence was hearsay-based. PW-2 and the seizure memos were contradictory, and the motorcycle colour evidence unreliable.
trial_duration: offence: 16.12.2012 (last seen together) and 17.12.2012 (bodies found); trial judgment: 14.05.2014; High Court: 30.04.2015; Supreme Court: 05.03.2019
legal_representation: Appellants: S. Nagamuthu, Senior Advocate, with Himanshu Agarwal, Ankita S., Ayush Raj Singh, Veerapan P. and Pyoli, Advocates. State: Atul Jha, Sandeep Jha and Dharmendra Kumar Sinha, Advocates.
investigation_status: FIR registered (Crime No.430/12, Police Station Bilaigarh); investigation completed; chargesheet filed; trial completed with 14 prosecution witnesses
procedural_irregularity: Key witness Anita not examined without explanation; three other children present not examined; fingerprint expert and sample-taker not examined; articles left at scene after lifting prints; unexplained delay in reporting the crime
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted, death sentence under s.302/34 IPC. High Court: death sentence confirmed, appeals dismissed. Supreme Court: appeals allowed, accused acquitted.
prosecution_argument: Supported the judgments of the courts below and prayed for dismissal of the appeals; no specific arguments recorded
defence_argument: Unexplained delay in reporting; child witness PW-8 uncorroborated and unreliable; s.27 recoveries (motorcycle, articles) unconnected and unreliable; PW-9 testimony hearsay; fingerprint report unreliable; last seen evidence insufficient
legal_principle_applied: Burden of proof on prosecution; suspicion cannot replace proof; circumstantial evidence chain must be complete (Jaharlal Das conditions); where two views are possible, the view favourable to the accused is adopted; child witness evidence needs corroboration as prudence; s.27 requires relevant discovery; last seen together requires close proximity
precedent_relied_upon: Jaharlal Das v. State of Orissa (1991) 3 SCC 27; Varkey Joseph v. State of Kerala 1993 Suppl (3) SCC 745; Sujit Biswas v. State of Assam (2013) 12 SCC 406; Kali Ram v. State of Himachal Pradesh (1973) 2 SCC 808; Panchhi v. State of U.P. (1998) 7 SCC 177; State of U.P. v. Ashok Dixit (2000) 3 SCC 70; State of Rajasthan v. Om Prakash (2002) 5 SCC 745; Alagupandi v. State of Tamil Nadu (2012) 10 SCC 451; Arjun Marik v. State of Bihar 1994 Supp (2) SCC 372; Kanhaiya Lal v. State of Rajasthan (2014) 4 SCC 715
other_sentence_order: Release forthwith unless required in any other case; High Court and Sessions Court judgments set aside
